claims.statement: useGame opens a single useStream on the `chess` assistant per game, and every submit carries configurable set to exactly the ChessContext fields, run_name chess-web with tag web, metadata surface web, and multitaskStrategy reject.

The web UI stores the current game's thread id in the `thread` URL query parameter via history.replaceState; when useStream reports a new thread id and the hook is still mounted, it persists the game's side and context to localStorage under langchain-chess:game:<threadId> and writes the id to the URL.

On load, App reopens the thread found in the URL with its stored side and context; a new game or rematch clears the URL thread and increments the seat number that keys the Table, remounting it so useStream starts a fresh thread, and a seat where the human plays Black auto-sends `go` once on mount guarded by a ref.

Human commands get message ids memoized by the key threadId:ply:content, so a resend of the same command at the same position reuses the id, which the server treats as a no-op for already-consumed ids.

useGame's play sends the UCI move as a human message with an optimistic pendingMove shown until the submit settles, start sends `go`, and retry submits empty input to resume a pending turn because a fresh `go` is rejected while a turn is pending.

The Table locks the board when viewing an earlier ply, while loading, after the game ends, while a turn is pending, or while an optimistic move is in flight, and it swallows the SDK's 'a run is already in flight' rejection while surfacing other submit errors.

Auth failures (HTTP 401/403 or matching text) show a banner directing the user to Settings, where the only app-level setting is the LangSmith API key stored under langchain-chess:app and passed to useStream.

Pressing Play in the New game dialog first checks the API key by POSTing to /assistants/search: 401/403 is 'missing' without a key and 'rejected' with one, a network failure is 'unreachable', and anything else is ok; the game starts only on ok and a late answer after unmount is ignored.

matchupOf derives the policy from the dialog picks (hybrid with both System 1 and an LLM, otherwise systemone or llm), rejects picking neither, an empty custom model spec, or an LLM game with memory summarize while the model's limit is still being checked, downgrades summarize to none for a model without a known limit, and fills the unused model field with its default; a Random side is resolved once when Play is pressed.
With no game on screen the New game dialog cannot be closed, and opening Settings from it preserves the unsaved picks as a draft that is restored on return.

The server exposes GET /ui/config returning the graph id, JSON schema and defaults of ChessContext, but the web client does not fetch it; context types, ranges and defaults are hand-mirrored in chess-ui types.ts and web settings.ts CONTEXT_CHECKS.

Stored context, setup and game records are treated as untrusted: each field or knob that fails validation falls back to its default individually, the removed memory value `full` is mapped to `summarize`, and legacy global settings and side-only game entries are migrated.

apiUrl uses VITE_API_URL if set, otherwise http://localhost:2024 in dev, otherwise the page origin; the production web build uses base /ui/ and outputs into the Python server package's static directory, which the server mounts at /ui.

packages/chess-ui is a private package whose exports point at TypeScript source (src/index.ts, styles.css, testing.ts) with no build step, so consuming apps compile it and must include its source in their Tailwind content globs and import its stylesheet.

chess-ui's ChessValues lists the only thread channels a UI may read (messages, start_fen, moves, plies, turns, outcome, error); positions are rebuilt client-side by replaying moves, stopping silently at the first move chess.js rejects because the server is authoritative.

liveAnalysis returns the latest AI text after the current turn opened (or after the last human message), skipping AI messages already committed as a ply's message, so a previous move's analysis is never shown as live.

apps/review is built as a single dependency-free CommonJS bundle exporting render(data, container, metadata) for the LangSmith custom-app sandbox, with code splitting disabled and NODE_ENV defined as production; render creates the root and stylesheet once and re-renders in place.

The review app talks only to the LangSmith API through window.langsmith.call: it lists projects, queries threads by project and time window in pages of 20, then fetches the threads' last root runs and game_review feedback in parallel and joins them into games.

reviewsByRun only accepts feedback with key game_review whose feedback_source metadata grader is 'lcchess grade' and whose value is a version-1 review with evals and plies arrays; other feedback under the key is ignored.
A review game's values are the last root run's outputs only when they contain a moves array; otherwise the app shows 'No game record', and ungraded games show a hint to run lcchess grade --thread.

GameView marks move-list entries with graded quality, draws the played move and the engine's differing best move as arrows, and shows an eval bar, grade card and eval graph from the review's per-position evals.
The review App tags each loaded games page with its project and since query so a stale response is never displayed for a newer query.

The pnpm workspace contains apps/web, apps/review and packages/*, with shared dependency versions pinned in a catalog (vite aliased to vite-plus-core) and referenced as catalog: so packages cannot drift.

Lint and format are configured only in the root vite.config.ts because Vite+ ignores nested lint/fmt blocks; lint is type-aware oxlint with rules-of-hooks and prefer-vite-plus-imports, and formatting ignores apps/server, libs and openwiki.

The web and review apps run jsdom Vitest over tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} with 100% line, function, branch and statement coverage thresholds; the review app writes coverage outside its directory because langsmith apps push ignores .gitignore.

Web tests replace useStream with a shared fake that records options and supports per-thread overrides, and App accepts injectable random, checkKey and modelLimit so tests are deterministic without a server.

The New game dialog asks the server for the chosen LLM's input limit via GET /ui/model-limit (debounced 300 ms, sending x-api-key when set), treating non-OK responses, malformed bodies and network errors as null; the summarize memory option is offered only when the limit is known and late answers for a no-longer-selected model are ignored.
